title: The full test run never fails on a video check that passes alone
goal: Two video checks fail now and then in a full test run and pass on their own, so a green release can still need a second run: the busy-video size estimate lands about a quarter off what it said, and a cut export now and then gets no picture from its recording for 30 seconds. Either the check reads something the rest of the suite changes, or the app has a real problem under load; find out which and fix it. A third such check, the moving Aurora title background, drew a different frame in playback than in scrubbing and export once during a full run.
notes:
Seen while measuring the-full-test-run-never-fails-on-a-speed-budget, 2026-10-30, in about 25 full Scripts/test.sh runs on this Mac (16 cores, go loop idle):
- BusyVideoSizeTests.swift:251 (A long recording that is quiet and then busy is weighed from stretches of it): near(landed 2102302, weighed 1597442) failed, once.
- BusyVideoSizeTests.swift:148 (Where the budget cannot hold, what the sheet weighs is what lands, speed 900): near(landed 1712276, weighed 1339509) failed, once.
- VideoCutExportTests.swift:35 (Exporting a recording with the middle dropped writes only what is left): Caught error .readerGaveUp("no picture came out of the recording for 30 seconds"), once.
Both BusyVideoSizeTests are in the .serialized run (Scripts/test.sh side run). Command: Scripts/test.sh with no arguments; output lines above are verbatim from those runs. Neither is a speed budget, so they were left out of the speed-budget task.
acceptance: Each failure is reproduced or explained: what about a busy machine makes the weighed size miss what lands, and what holds the reader for 30 seconds.
Neither check fails in ten full Scripts/test.sh runs in a row on this Mac.
A real defect in the app found on the way (an estimate that is wrong under load, a reader that stalls) is fixed, not loosened in the test.

The Aurora and Behind Glass check (TitleBackgroundsRenderTests: playback, scrubbing and export draw the same frames) also passes 20 full Scripts/test.sh runs in a row, or its difference is shown to be GPU rounding with numbers and bounded to 1 level per pixel

log.note: Seen twice in a row on 2026-10-31 ~16:40 (Scripts/test.sh, no model loaded, nothing over 30% CPU): VideoCutExportTests.swift:92 'The frame reader tells a cut recording from an uncut one' (82s, readerGaveUp 'no picture came out of the recording for 30 seconds'), then VideoAssetCommitTests.swift:104 aSavedRecordingReadsAsCleanAndRecordsHowItWasDerived (35s, same error). VideoCutExportTests alone: 7 tests pass in 2.1s. The change under test only touched change_part's colour maths in PhotonzCore.

2026-11-01, seen again by five-more-arrow-styles: full Scripts/test.sh failed only on BusyVideoSizeTests (quiet-then-busy recording: landed 2148882 vs weighed 1597442; long still-then-busy document: landed 2358656 vs weighed 1778932); Scripts/test.sh --filter BusyVideoSize passed 8/8 alone right after.

triage 2026-11-02: folded in a-moving-aurora-title-background-draws-the-same (dropped as a near-twin). A third check that fails only inside a full run: in the v0.22.0 release preflight (2026-11-01) TitleBackgroundsRenderTests 'Playback, scrubbing and export draw the same Aurora and Behind Glass frames' failed with 'Aurora: scrub differs at 3640' and 'Aurora: export differs at 3640' (TitleBackgroundsRenderTests.swift:307-308); the full suite passed on the rerun. Spot-checked 2026-11-02: Scripts/test.sh --filter TitleBackgroundsRenderTests passed 3 of 3 alone (7 tests, 3.6 s each). Leads: Aurora is .live, drawn by LiveBackdropPainter.image through the live_aurora kernel in DocumentRenderer.driftingFill; check for a Core Image device or precision fallback under load, a cache evicted mid-playback, or a clock leaking into the kernel. If it is GPU rounding, bound it (no pixel more than 1 level apart) rather than let it flake.
